text:
Architectural precedent is strong: [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781) already adaptively combines historical interactions, so adding a recent-window branch does not by itself establish long/short-term disentanglement. [HGN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.09217) combines long-term user interests, feature/instance-gated recent-item representations, and explicit item–item interactions; [TLSRec](https://yneversky.github.io/Papers/cikm22.pdf) uses dimension-wise gating to fuse separately modeled long- and short-term preferences. A SASRec-plus-recent-mean residual is therefore best framed as a lightweight fusion variant. [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) supplies initialization precedent: a zero-initialized residual coefficient preserves the starting function exactly. For h + sigmoid(b)·r, zero bias instead gives a substantial 0.5 residual weight; b≈−3 gives ≈0.047. These are mathematical consequences, not demonstrated recommendation-specific optima. Normalizing the residual branch preserves h when its coefficient is zero; applying a new LayerNorm after addition generally changes h even with the branch disabled.

Recommended controls, rather than reported findings: compare unchanged SASRec, recent-mean-only scoring, last-item-only scoring, fixed residual coefficients, a learned global scalar, and an input-dependent sigmoid gate under identical validation conditions. Match residual addition against convex mixing while controlling representation norms, since score-scale changes can confound fusion effects. Sweep window size, including one item and the full available history; compare uniform pooling with recency-weighted pooling. Use padding-masked, causal windows at every training position. Inspect gate variation, saturation, branch norms, and validation HR@10 by history length and category. Gains over a tuned fixed coefficient establish value from adaptive gating; gains over pooling alone establish value from the sequential encoder. Neither alone demonstrates distinct long- and short-term interests.
